# Perfect Six

## #0 — Choose the divisor operation

A positive integer is perfect when it equals the sum of its positive proper divisors. The [core spine, §III](../../episteme/sources/internal-corpus/taylor/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy/taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md) takes 6 through a broader counting unit. This page isolates the exact divisor construction before returning it to the native field.

The inputs are the integer 6 and ordinary positive divisibility. “Proper” excludes 6 itself; zero and negative divisors are not included in this definition.

## #1 — Enumerate the divisors

The positive integers below 6 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Testing divisibility leaves 1, 2, 3: `6=1·6=2·3=3·2`. Neither 4 nor 5 divides 6. Their sum is `1+2+3=6`, so 6 is perfect.

It is the smallest positive perfect number. For 1 the proper-divisor sum is 0; for 2, 3, 4, 5 the sums are respectively 1, 1, 3, 1. This finite check proves the minimality claim without a general classification theorem.

## #2 — Compare the product separately

The same triple also satisfies `1×2×3=6`. Addition and multiplication therefore converge on 6 for this particular input. This equality is not the definition of perfection:28 has proper divisors 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, whose sum is 28 but whose product is 784.

The native additive/multiplicative hinge is carried by the selected triple, with its special relation preserved. Extending the list changes the operation: adding 4 gives 10, while multiplying by 4 gives 24.

## #3 — Introduce zero without changing its office silently

`0+1+2+3=6`, while `0×1×2×3=0`. Zero is the additive identity and multiplicative absorbing element. The core reads this as the two faces of a contextual boundary: one permits the determined sum, the other dissolves the product.

Modulo 6, the number 6 is congruent to 0. This is a separate quotient operation; it does not change integer 6 into integer 0. The [number quilt](../quilt/number.md) places perfection, operator bifurcation and modular return in the sixfold sequence.

## #4 — Relate the count to the native body

The binary self-relation gives `2+2²=6`; the divisor sum gives `1+2+3=6`. Their cardinal results coincide under distinct constructions. Mapping them into one six-position display requires the native positional relation, not just the shared numeral.

The [tetraktys and triangle](tetraktys-triangle.md) adds other exact counts and measures: triangular 10, area 6 and perimeter 12. Their relation to qualitative or historical Pythagorean meanings remains separate from these arithmetic proofs.

## #5→0 — Return the perfect number to its operation

The result is 6 with an exact earned property and a further sum/product coincidence. Its native role can now be read without turning every occurrence of six into the same theorem or treating “perfect” as a universal judgement of value.
